body:
Why practices need AI before the next EOFY

Accounting work is seasonal and deadline-driven. Every BAS quarter and every EOFY, teams spend hours chasing clients for documents, sorting attachments, keying data and answering the same questions. Skilled accountants end up doing admin, and capacity limits how many clients a practice can take on.

AI takes over the collection, sorting and data entry, so your team spends its time reviewing, advising and growing client relationships.

Where AI helps accounting firms most

Document collection and chasing

Clients receive personal requests for exactly what is missing, with polite reminders until it arrives. Uploaded files are sorted into the right client folder automatically. See AI workflow automation.

Invoice and receipt processing

AI reads supplier invoices and receipts, extracts ABN, GST and amounts, and prepares draft entries in Xero or MYOB for review. See document & data processing.

Deadline reminders

BAS, IAS, tax return and EOFY reminders go out on schedule, personalised to each client’s obligations. See CRM automation.

Client questions

A chatbot or inbox assistant answers common questions such as which documents to provide or how to use your portal, from your approved content. See AI chatbot development.

Practice admin

New client onboarding, engagement letters and job status updates run automatically. See business process automation.

Human-backed AI employees for accounting firms

Most accounting firms don’t want another tool to supervise. Our AI Employees service builds the AI around your practice, then runs it with a dedicated Crenosoft team that learns your services, clients and rules. The AI handles routine work; our reviewers handle anything unusual, around the clock; and decisions that belong to you come to your nominated person with a clear summary. We agree an hours-saved target up front and report against it every month.

Software we connect to

We connect with Xero, Xero Practice Manager, MYOB, FYI, Karbon, Ignition and similar practice tools, plus email, client portals, e-signature and document storage such as SharePoint and Google Drive.

Professional standards and client confidentiality

AI supports registered practitioners; it doesn’t replace their judgement. Advice, tax positions and lodgements are always reviewed and approved by your team, consistent with the Code of Professional Conduct overseen by the Tax Practitioners Board. Client financial information stays in controlled systems with access limited by role, and providers are configured so data isn’t used for model training where that option exists.

Across every project we follow the Privacy Act 1988, the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products and our own Responsible AI Policy.

What changes for your team

Instead of starting each job by chasing documents and keying data, your accountants start with a complete, organised file and draft entries ready to review. Juniors spend less time on data entry and more on learning to analyse and advise. Partners get earlier visibility of which clients are ready and which are holding up the queue, which makes the busy season far more predictable.

Results we measure for practices

Before we build, we record a baseline of how long the work takes and how often it happens. After launch, your monthly report tracks the numbers that matter to practices:

  • Documents collected without manual chasing
  • Invoices and receipts processed into Xero or MYOB
  • Client reminders sent and deadlines met
  • Staff hours saved during BAS and EOFY
  • Accuracy from review samples

These figures sit alongside hours saved and accuracy, so you can see exactly what the AI is contributing and where our team is still stepping in.

Because the AI follows the same rules for every client, document requests and reminders are consistent across the whole practice, no matter which team member owns the client. That consistency also makes it easier to onboard new staff before the busy season.

Many practices also use the same workflows year-round for monthly bookkeeping clients, so the investment keeps paying back well beyond tax season.

How to get started

  1. Free AI audit: 30 minutes to map your busiest workflows and pick the first opportunity.
  2. Blueprint and fixed quote: what the AI will do, which systems it connects to and the price in AUD.
  3. Build and test: usually two to six weeks, tested on real examples from your practice.
  4. Launch and improve: monthly reports on hours saved, accuracy and improvements.

Not sure where to begin? Start with an AI Readiness Assessment, or see how we work locally on our Melbourne AI agency page.
faqs: Can AI enter data into Xero?
Yes. AI can extract invoice and receipt details and create draft bills or transactions in Xero for your team to review and approve.
Will AI give tax advice to clients?
No. AI answers routine admin questions from your approved content. Tax advice and positions always come from your registered practitioners.
Can AI chase clients for missing documents?
Yes. It sends personalised requests for the exact items missing and follows up until they arrive, then files them in the right place.
Ideally a few months before EOFY, so document collection and processing workflows are tested before the busiest period.
